stories.title: SRS Closes Sale of Newly Built Caliber Collision Property
stories.excerpt: SRS Real Estate Partners has completed the $5.24-million sale of a Caliber Collision property located at 742 Main Street in Chula Vista. The 16,832-square-foot property recently completed construction and has a 15-year corporate-guaranteed absolute triple net lease in place. SRS Capital Markets Senior Managing Principals Matthew Mousavi and Patrick Luther and Vice President Greg Labarre represented the seller, a Southern California-based developer.  The buyer was a family trust from Southern California. The property is part of a new development that will feature Starbucks, Quick Quack Car Wash, Taco Bell, Circle K, and Chipotle, among other recognizable brands, all being separately marketed and available for sale by SRS with a total value of approximately $30 million. It is less than one mile from Interstate 805 and Chula Vista Crossings, a Kohl’s-anchored retail center. “This property had a significant amount of investor interest and sold over the asking price, which was a 5.5% cap rate,” said Luther. “This long-term tenant is poised to do significant business as it is located near multiple auto dealerships and auto service retailers and is in a densely populated area with more than 348,200 residents, and 81,200 employees within a one-mile radius.” Mousavi added, “This was an ideal, fee-simple, low-maintenance opportunity for the new owner as it presents minimal property management responsibilities.” The post SRS Closes Sale of Newly Built Caliber Collision Property appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: SRS sold $5.24M Caliber Collision property, Chula Vista at 5.5% cap rate.
348,200 residents and 81,200 employees within one-mile radius of I-805.
Multi-tenant development (~$30M total) includes Starbucks, Taco Bell, Quick Quack Car Wash.
stories.summary: SRS Real Estate Partners closed the $5.24 million sale of a newly built Caliber Collision property in Chula Vista near I-805 to a family trust at a 5.5% cap rate, exceeding asking price. The property is part of a larger $30 million mixed-use development featuring national retail and QSR brands. The submarket offers dense demographics (348,200 residents, 81,200 employees within one mile) with proximity to auto dealerships and the Chula Vista Crossings retail center.
stories.impact: Tight cap rates (5.5%) and strong investor appetite for newly built commercial reflect investor confidence in coastal Southern California suburban infill near major corridors. For multifamily developers in San Diego County, this signals healthy market fundamentals and investor capital deployment in dense residential submarkets; competition for sites near I-805 and retail anchors will intensify.

stories.title: NAI Hanson Tapped to Lease former Barnes & Noble Headquarters
stories.excerpt: NAI James E. Hanson announced that SVPs W. Joshua Levering, SIOR, and Charles Laginestra, and associate Chris D’Andrea, have been tapped by First National Realty Management, LLC, as the exclusive leasing team for 120 Mountainview Blvd. in Basking Ridge, NJ. The former world headquarters of Barnes & Noble, 120 Mountainview features a two-story lobby, an onsite cafe, outdoor seating, a bocce court, over 500 on-site parking spaces, and more. The property also offers a location near Interstates 78 and 287, providing access to Newark Liberty International Airport, New York City and Somerset County’s corporate corridor. “This is a rare opportunity to secure a large block of Class-A space in one of the state’s most established corporate corridors,” said Levering. “With new ownership that is experienced and fully committed to reinvesting in the property, 120 Mountainview is perfectly suited for users seeking a striking headquarters that offers flexibility, connectivity, responsive ownership, and a full suite of premium amenities.” The post NAI Hanson Tapped to Lease former Barnes & Noble Headquarters appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: NAI Hanson tapped to lease 120 Mountainview Blvd, former Barnes & Noble HQ, Basking Ridge, NJ.
Class-A property near I-78, I-287; access to Newark airport and NYC.
Property offers 500+ parking spaces, two-story lobby, cafe, outdoor amenities.
stories.summary: First National Realty Management engaged NAI James E. Hanson to exclusively lease 120 Mountainview Boulevard in Basking Ridge, New Jersey, the former worldwide headquarters of Barnes & Noble. The Class-A property sits in an established corporate corridor near I-78 and I-287 with convenient access to Newark Liberty International Airport, New York City, and Somerset County's corporate office market. The building features premium amenities including 500+ parking spaces, a two-story lobby, on-site cafe, and outdoor seating.
stories.impact: Corporate headquarters repositioning signals potential office-to-multifamily conversion opportunity if leasing struggles persist; Basking Ridge's proximity to Newark/NYC and suburban corporate corridor makes it a bellwether for Northeast suburban office demand. Multifamily developers should monitor leasing velocity—weakened office fundamentals could open land/building acquisition windows in this affluent, job-rich submarket.

stories.title: Starwood Lands $483M CMBS Loan to Refi Single-Family Rental Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Barry Sternlicht’s Starwood Asset Management secured a $482.5 million commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) loan to refinance a nearly full single-family rental portfolio located across 10 states. The floating-rate, interest-only financing — which Japan’s Nomura Securities originated — backs 1,749 properties, according to Fitch Ratings. The debt, which is scheduled to mature in August 2028, has three 12-month extension options. The portfolio was just over 96 percent leased in April. On average, the homes span 1,812 square feet and date back to 1992. Starwood Asset Management paid $674 million for the houses, assembling the portfolio between 2021 and 2022. Nearly a third are located in Georgia, followed by nearly a quarter in Arizona and just under 12 percent in Florida. Within Palm Beach County, there are 27 homes, most of which are located in Lake Worth, according to property records. The debt comes as Starwood has been making other multifamily inroads, buying four affordable housing properties across Miami-Dade County just last week for a combined $115 million. For Nomura, the financing marks a sizable loan since re-entering the U.S. market last year after a 27-year hiatus. A division of Nomura Group, one of Japan’s major financial institutions, the firm had helped pioneer the CMBS scheme back in the 1990s. Representatives for Starwood declined to comment, while representatives for Nomura did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Starwood Asset Management secured $482.5M CMBS loan for 1,749 single-family rental homes across 10 states.
Portfolio 96% leased; 31% in Georgia, 24% in Arizona, 12% in Florida.
Starwood paid $674M for portfolio (2021–2022); financing matures August 2028 with extension options.
stories.summary: Barry Sternlicht's Starwood Asset Management obtained a $482.5 million floating-rate, interest-only CMBS loan (originated by Nomura Securities) to refinance a 1,749-property single-family rental portfolio across 10 states, maturing in August 2028 with three 12-month extension options. The portfolio, acquired between 2021 and 2022 for $674 million, was nearly 96% leased in April; largest concentrations are Georgia (31%), Arizona (24%), and Florida (12%), with 27 homes in Palm Beach County. Starwood simultaneously acquired four affordable housing properties in Miami-Dade County.
stories.impact: Successful SFR securitization at scale signals lender confidence in rental housing fundamentals and refinancing availability for bulk portfolios despite floating-rate risk. For multifamily developers, this demonstrates investor and debt appetite for residential across Sunbelt growth markets (GA, AZ, FL); competition for land and development sites in these high-volume markets will remain intense, and cap rates on acquisitions may compress if SFR operators expand aggressively.

stories.title: Wrentham Village Adds to Extensive Lineup of Outlet Stores, Dining Options
stories.excerpt: Wrentham Village Premium Outlets, New England’s largest outdoor outlet shopping destination, is expanding its portfolio of diverse brands, with HARIBO recently holding its grand opening. Arc’teryx Factory Outlet and Gong Cha will follow later this month. The Wrentham Village location is one of the first U.S. retail outlets for HARIBO, a German confectionery brand. Zwilling Factory Outlet and Birkenstock will be the next stores to open in September. They join a lineup of more than 150 brands and dining options. “August is shaping up to be one of our biggest months yet,” said Ashley Feldhouse, Area Director of Marketing and Business Development. “Welcoming HARIBO to New England with a full weekend of grand opening festivities shows just how much momentum we’re building at Wrentham Village Premium Outlets. With Arc’teryx and Gong Cha right behind them, plus Birkenstock and Zwilling on the way this September, there’s truly something for every guest to discover in the months ahead.” The post Wrentham Village Adds to Extensive Lineup of Outlet Stores, Dining Options appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Wrentham Village Premium Outlets expanding with HARIBO, Arc'teryx, Gong Cha, Birkenstock, Zwilling openings.
150+ brand outlet destination in New England; located 30+ miles south of Boston.
Momentum indicates retail leasing strength; no supply-side constraint evident.
stories.summary: Wrentham Village Premium Outlets, New England's largest outlet shopping destination, announced multiple brand openings including HARIBO (one of its first U.S. outlets), Arc'teryx Factory Outlet, Gong Cha, Birkenstock, and Zwilling Factory Outlet throughout August and September. The center now hosts over 150 brands and dining options. Described as experiencing strong leasing momentum with August characterized as "one of our biggest months yet."
stories.impact: Limited direct relevance to multifamily development; this is outlet retail expansion in a mature, non-urban location. Retail leasing strength in suburban New England may indicate sustained consumer spending and regional economic confidence, which could support residential demand in commuter-shed towns, but no specific demographic migration or job creation is signaled.

stories.title: Extell Finalizes Deal to Buy 110 East 55th Street for $65M
stories.excerpt: After months of negotiations, Extell Development has acquired 110 East 55th Street, a 19-story Midtown office property also known as Park 55, from the Parkoff Organization for $65 million, property records made public Monday show. An affiliate of construction company JT Magen — which had previously partnered with Extell on a foreclosure in Boston — filed a pre-foreclosure suit at the property in May, The Real Deal reported. The foreclosure complaint alleged that Parkoff defaulted on a loan and owed some $40.6 million in principal and interest. Parkoff and Extell did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s requests for comment. Extell founder Gary Barnett was reported to be in contract for the property back in January, but a sales price was never reported until the deal closed this week. Now, Barnett will add the building to his firm’s ever-growing collection of Midtown-based assets. Most recently, Extell acquired a block-long development site at 405-417 Park Avenue in May for $500 million, CO previously reported. The site — which has the potential for upwards of 700,000 square feet of rentable office space — went up for sale in August of last year. Extell also acquired the Friars Club building at 57 East 55th Street for $19 million in late April. Additionally, Barnett secured 123,000 square feet of air rights over Saint Thomas Church at 678 Fifth Avenue for $36 million last year. It’s unclear exactly what Barnett has planned for his massive Midtown assemblage — which is also set to include 111 East 54th Street — but the developer is already busy with other development projects in Manhattan. The firm has several Midtown developments in the works, including a 600-foot-tall office tower at 570 Fifth Avenue, a 1,200-foot residential tower at 77 West 66th Street, a 70-story condominium at 50 West 66th Street, a 71-story mixed-use tower at 871 Seventh Avenue — the former Wellington Hotel — and a 1,162-foot-tall residential skyscraper at 655 Madison Avenue. bullets: Extell Development acquired 110 East 55th Street (Park 55), 19-story Midtown office, for $65M.
Property was distressed; JT Magen filed pre-foreclosure suit in May; Parkoff defaulted on ~$40.6M debt.
Extell also acquired 405–417 Park Avenue development site for $500M in May (700k+ SF potential).
stories.summary: Extell Development closed acquisition of 110 East 55th Street (Park 55), a 19-story Midtown Manhattan office building, for $65 million from the Parkoff Organization following months of negotiation. The property had been in financial distress; an affiliate of construction company JT Magen filed a pre-foreclosure suit in May alleging Parkoff defaulted on a loan with ~$40.6 million in principal and interest owed. This acquisition adds to Extell's growing Midtown portfolio, which includes the $500 million block-long acquisition at 405–417 Park Avenue announced in May.
stories.impact: Distressed office sales and Extell's aggressive acquisition strategy signal ongoing Manhattan office market pressure and founder Gary Barnett's conviction in conversion potential. For multifamily developers, successful office acquisitions by residential-focused operators (especially at distressed prices) reduce available land/building supply for new-build multifamily and may accelerate conversion/redevelopment pipelines; this intensifies competition for Midtown sites and favors operators with strong balance sheets and conversion expertise.

stories.title: Chipotle, Starbucks to Open at Pullman Gateway Complex
stories.excerpt: Pullman Gateway has achieved full occupancy, completing the transformation of a long-vacant property into a mixed-use destination developed and fully leased in just over two years. The grand opening of a 1,500-square-foot Chipotle Mexican Grill with a drive-thru at 11211 South Corliss Avenue marks the completion of the eight-acre development. The celebration also marked the announcement of another major commercial investment in the community. Plans call for the new Pullman Park Retail Center, a commercial development anchored by Starbucks, Tropical Smoothie Café, and Slim & Husky’s Pizza Beeria. Slim & Husky’s will be the Nashville-based pizza company’s first Chicago location, with former Chicago Bear Matt Forte as a significant investor.Together, Pullman Gateway and the new Pullman Park Retail Center, developed by Chicago Neighborhood Initiatives, represent the next phase of sustained investment. Located at 112th Street and South Corliss Avenue, Pullman Gateway has transformed a former Hawthorne Racecourse off-track betting facility and underutilized parking lot into a mixed-use development featuring Chick-fil-A, Dunkin’ and Jimmy John’s, along with CTA offices supporting construction of the Red Line Extension. The post Chipotle, Starbucks to Open at Pullman Gateway Complex appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Pullman Gateway (Chicago, 8-acre mixed-use) achieved full occupancy in ~2 years; Chipotle drive-thru opened.
Pullman Park Retail Center anchored by Starbucks, Tropical Smoothie, Slim & Husky's (Nashville pizza, Matt Forte investor).
Redevelopment of former Hawthorne Racecourse site; sustained neighborhood investment phase.
stories.summary: Pullman Gateway, an eight-acre mixed-use development on Chicago's South Side, achieved full occupancy in just over two years with the grand opening of a 1,500-square-foot Chipotle with drive-thru at 11211 South Corliss Avenue. Concurrently, developers (Chicago Neighborhood Initiatives) announced Pullman Park Retail Center, a commercial development anchored by Starbucks, Tropical Smoothie Café, and Slim & Husky's Pizza Beeria (Nashville-based brand's first Chicago location, backed by former Chicago Bear Matt Forte). Both projects represent the next phase of sustained investment in a redeveloped area.
stories.impact: Rapid fill-up of mixed-use commercial and QSR anchor activity in South Chicago signals strong neighborhood demand momentum and successful placemaking. For multifamily developers, this represents a submarket emerging from underinvestment; nearby residential development (rental or for-sale) would benefit from established retail ecosystems and job/foot-traffic corridors. Monitor absorption rates and consider South Side sites near Pullman Gateway for transit-oriented or lifestyle-oriented multifamily.

stories.title: Co-Working Provider Canopy Signs Full-Building Lease at Long-Vacant Presidio Structure
stories.excerpt: The Presidio Trust has signed a 40,000-square-foot lease with Canopy, a boutique co-working and flexible office provider, for the full building at 102 Montgomery St. It is the last historic brick structure on the Presidio’s Main Post to be restored and activated, and one of the largest leases signed in the San Francisco landmark complex this year. Originally constructed in 1896, the building had been vacant since the 1970s. Following an 18-month, full-scale rehabilitation by the Trust, the property has been brought back to life for modern use. The new Canopy location, which joins three others in San Francisco, is expected to open in the spring of 2027. “We’re very pleased to welcome CANOPY to the Presidio,” said Daryl Ansel, interim director of commercial asset management, Presidio Trust. “Creating places where people can work, connect, and engage with the park strengthens the Presidio’s vitality and supports a dynamic tenant community.” The post Co-Working Provider Canopy Signs Full-Building Lease at Long-Vacant Presidio Structure appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Canopy co-working leased full 40,000 SF historic building at Presidio, San Francisco (102 Montgomery St).
Building vacant since 1970s; underwent 18-month full restoration; opening Spring 2027.
Canopy's 4th San Francisco location; one of largest leases at Presidio this year.
stories.summary: The Presidio Trust signed a 40,000-square-foot full-building lease with Canopy, a boutique co-working and flexible office provider, for 102 Montgomery Street, a historic brick structure originally built in 1896 and vacant since the 1970s. Following an 18-month comprehensive restoration, the property will open as Canopy's fourth San Francisco location in spring 2027, marking one of the largest leases signed at the Presidio complex this year.
stories.impact: Limited direct relevance to multifamily development; this is flex/co-working office leasing in a historic landmark park setting. However, the Presidio's activation and amenity-rich positioning may eventually support surrounding residential demand, particularly if the site draws young professional or creative-class tenants seeking work-live proximity. Monitor whether successful activation attracts residential development interest in or near the Presidio campus.

stories.title: Terreno Realty Acquires Red Hook Warehouse for $26M
stories.excerpt: Terreno Realty has acquired a warehouse along the Red Hook, Brooklyn, waterfront. Terreno announced Monday the purchase of the 28,000-square-foot industrial property at 659 Court Street for $26.3 million from California-based LBA Properties, which made a pretty penny since buying it less thana year and a half ago for $7 million, according to property records. The building sits right on the banks of the East River with parking for 70 cars and two loading bays, according to the buyers. The warehouse is also leased to a maritime goods and services provider. It’s unclear who brokered the deal. LBA did not immediately respond to a request for comment, while Terreno did not immediately respond to a request for additional comment. With 145,800 square feet of buildable space with the addition of air rights, the price for the property has fluctuated dramatically over the years. Buckeye Partners, which sold the property to LBA in March 2025, acquired it themselves in 2013 for $15.5 million, but paid $92.1 million in a real property transfer tax in late 2019, according to property records. The transaction follows on strong leasing fundamentals reported in the industrial sector in the second quarter of 2026. CBRE clocked leasing at an 11 percent increase year-over-year to 268.7 million square feet across the U.S., while vacancies dropped to 6.5 percent, according to the report. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Terreno Realty acquired Red Hook warehouse, Brooklyn, 28,000 SF, for $26.3M from LBA Properties.
Seller profited 275% in <18 months (bought $7M, sold $26.3M); maritime tenant leased.
Property on East River waterfront with 70-car parking, 2 loading bays; 145,800 SF buildable with air rights.
stories.summary: Terreno Realty purchased a 28,000-square-foot waterfront warehouse at 659 Court Street in Red Hook, Brooklyn, for $26.3 million from California-based LBA Properties, which acquired it less than 18 months prior for $7 million—a 275% profit. The property sits on the East River with parking for 70 vehicles, two loading bays, and is leased to a maritime goods and services provider. With 145,800 square feet of buildable space when including air rights, the property has seen significant price appreciation over recent years.
stories.impact: Explosive waterfront industrial price appreciation (LBA 275% in <18 months) signals scarcity of Brooklyn waterfront land and strong investor demand for conversion-eligible industrial assets. For multifamily developers, Red Hook's limited remaining developable waterfront sites and rising land costs will compress feasibility on new projects; consider acquisition of industrial sites for residential conversion if feasible, but expect competitive bidding and higher basis. Proximity to Manhattan and transit make this a high-demand submarket—monitor for adaptive-reuse or residential development opportunities.

stories.title: Aircraft Finance Firm Buys Florida HQ Complex For $118M
stories.excerpt: A publicly traded aircraft finance firm has paid $118 million for a three-building, 375,000-square-foot campus under construction in Coconut Creek, Fla. disclosed the transaction and purchase price in a public filing this month. The Coconut Creek-based company bought Cocomar Business Park, under development at 4733, 4763 and 4851 West Atlantic Boulevard as its new corporate headquarters, the South Florida Business Journal reported. The company lists its current headquarters as 4700 Lyons Technology Parkway. The seller is an affiliate of Greystar of Charleston, S.C., which last year bought the site for $30.5 million. A marketing brochure said the industrial buildings include 32-foot ceilings, 78 dock doors and 313 parking spaces. Each building includes a small amount of office space and conference rooms. Completion of the 35-acre campus is expected in the third quarter of this year. In its most recent annual report, Willis Lease Finance said it owns its 60,000-square-foot headquarters in Coconut Creek and leases 45,000 square feet in Pompano Beach, Fla., and 25,000 square feet in Sunrise, Fla. The company reported 475 employees in the U.S., the United Kingdom, Ireland and elsewhere. As of the end of 2025, Willis Lease Finance owned 363 engines, 20 aircraft, one marine vessel and other leased parts and equipment leased out to 69 lessees in 37 countries. Jeff Ostrowski can be reached at jostrowski@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Willis Lease Finance (aircraft finance, publicly traded) bought Cocomar Business Park, Coconut Creek FL, for $118M.
375,000 SF campus of 3 buildings under construction; 35-acre site; completion Q3 2025.
Seller affiliate of Greystar; site acquired for $30.5M in 2024; includes 32-ft ceilings, 78 dock doors.
stories.summary: Willis Lease Finance Corporation, a publicly traded aircraft finance firm, acquired Cocomar Business Park, a three-building, 375,000-square-foot campus under construction in Coconut Creek, Florida, for $118 million as its new corporate headquarters. The 35-acre development at 4733, 4763, and 4851 West Atlantic Boulevard, being developed by a Greystar affiliate (which bought the site for $30.5 million in 2024), includes industrial-flex buildings with 32-foot ceilings, 78 dock doors, and 313 parking spaces; completion is expected in Q3 2025.
stories.impact: Corporate HQ consolidation and build-to-suit acquisition in Coconut Creek signals Broward County's appeal for back-office and operational headquarters, attracting institutional users. For multifamily developers, this demonstrates sustained commercial/industrial demand in the I-595 corridor northwest of Fort Lauderdale; surrounding residential submarkets should see supporting job growth and in-migration. Monitor for additional corporate relocations and build-to-suit projects; this could support rental demand in Coconut Creek, Deerfield Beach, and northern Broward multifamily markets.

stories.title: PGIM Sells Delray Beach Assisted Living Community for at Least $140M
stories.excerpt: PGIM Real Estate sold a relatively new assisted living facility in Delray Beach, Fla., for at least $140 million, marking one of the biggest South Florida retirement home sales in recent years. Chevy Chase, Md.-based Artemis Real Estate Partners purchased the 7.2-acre asset, property records show. The 224,951-square-foot community, called The Arbor at Delray, houses 207 apartments at 6595 Morikami Park Road, just west of South Jog Road. The complex includes a 35,586-square-foot recreational clubhouse and a 51,461-square-foot nursing home. The sale breaks down to just under $676,300 per unit, though it’s unclear whether the $140 million figure listed on the deed also includes the operations for the business, which could boost the price tag. PGIM Real Estate, part of insurance giant Prudential Financial, completed the property in 2023. Two years earlier, PGIM-backed Alliance Residential Company purchased the land for $8.2 million and secured a $45.7 million construction loan from Dallas-based Comerica Bank, The Real Deal reported. There’s been an uptick in the number of assisted living facilities across Palm Beach County this year as the occupancy rate in Florida neared 90 percent, with monthly rents averaging over $5,000 in the second quarter of 2026, according to data from Colliers. Just last week, Healthpeak Properties bought a 136-unit facility in Boynton Beach for at least $62 million. Representatives for Artemis and PGIM did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: PGIM Real Estate sold The Arbor at Delray Beach assisted living for ≥$140M to Artemis Real Estate Partners.
224,951 SF, 207 units, 7.2 acres; completed 2023; ~$676,300 per unit.
Property includes 35,586 SF clubhouse and 51,461 SF nursing home; one of largest South Florida senior sales.
stories.summary: PGIM Real Estate sold The Arbor at Delray Beach, a relatively new assisted living facility, for at least $140 million to Chevy Chase, Maryland-based Artemis Real Estate Partners, marking one of the largest South Florida retirement home sales in recent years. The 224,951-square-foot community on 7.2 acres at 6595 Morikami Park Road houses 207 apartments, a 35,586-square-foot recreational clubhouse, and a 51,461-square-foot nursing home, with a valuation of approximately $676,300 per unit. PGIM Real Estate, part of Prudential Financial, completed the property in 2023 after its affiliate purchased the land in 2021 for $8.2 million and secured $45.7 million in construction financing.
stories.impact: Strong exit valuation ($140M+) for 2-year-old senior housing reflects institutional investor appetite for Class-A age-restricted communities in South Florida's high-retirement-demand markets. For multifamily developers, this signals capital flow into senior housing and validates mixed-income/lifestyle-amenity strategies; Delray Beach's demographic profile (aging, affluent) makes it attractive for continued senior and 55+ development. Consider senior/age-restricted multifamily development in South Florida markets; competition from experienced operators (Artemis) will be significant.
